questiontext.text:
Rewrite the following equation in index form. \(\log_{@a@}{@b@}={@n@}\)

Enter your answer as an equation in index form.

generalfeedback.text:
Recall the relationship between logarithmic form and index form:

\(\log_a(b)=n \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad a^n=b.\)

In this question, the given equation is

\(\log_{@a@}{@b@}={@n@}.\)

To convert it into index form, follow these steps:

1. The base of the logarithm, {@a@}, becomes the base of the power.

2. The value of the logarithm, {@n@}, becomes the exponent.

3. The argument of the logarithm, {@b@}, becomes the result of the power.

Therefore, the equivalent equation in index form is

\({@a@}^{@n@}={@b@}.\)

Example: If the question displays \(\log_3(81)=4\), then the equivalent index form is \(3^4=81\).

Remember that a logarithm tells you the exponent to which the base must be raised to obtain the argument.
